claims.claim: For p not dividing the base b, collision detection is exactly repeated-state detection on mismatch-only normalized prefix sums. Moreover, every collision has a witness containing at most p mismatching aligned positions, although its length may exceed p.
claims.evidence: For displacement d and 0<=r<e<=n-d, multiplying A_d(e)-A_d(r) by b^e is valid because b is invertible modulo p and gives exactly F(r,e-r)-F(r+d,e-r). Equality of states is therefore equivalent to equal fingerprints, while an actual mismatch in [r,e) is equivalent to unequal contents. A_d changes only at mismatch positions q_j, so every relevant endpoint state is represented by B_0=0 or B_j=A_d(q_j+1). Conversely, B_a=B_c with a<c yields a colliding pair on [0,q_c+1) if a=0, or [q_a+1,q_c+1) otherwise, containing exactly c-a mismatches. If there are at least p mismatches, B_0,...,B_p contain p+1 values in a p-element field and hence repeat with at most p intervening mismatches. If there are fewer than p mismatches, every possible witness already has fewer than p.
claims.witness: A repeated pair B_a=B_c constructs the two unequal colliding substrings at displacement d using endpoints r=0 when a=0 and r=q_a+1 otherwise, and e=q_c+1; the witness contains c-a<=p mismatches.
claims.search_method: Independent algebraic derivation from the fingerprint definition, followed by exhaustive exact-integer comparison of all aligned intervals and mismatch-boundary states for bases 2 through 4, primes 2,3,5,7, and the tested lengths.

claims.claim: In the word-RAM model with p=n^{O(1)}, there is an exact deterministic algorithm running in O(n log n+n+min{D,M,n min(n,p)}) time, where D is the number of distinct substring contents and M is the number of unequal unordered character-position pairs. Consequently the requested O(n log n) bound holds when p=O(log n), D=O(n log n), or M=O(n log n).
claims.evidence: Deterministic suffix-array/LCP/RMQ preprocessing supplies constant-time LCE queries in O(n log n). For each displacement d, LCE jumps visit only mismatches. Encountering p mismatches permits immediate acceptance by claim 0; otherwise the algorithm records all mismatch-boundary states and detects equality after radix sorting by (d,state). The record count is Q<=(n-1)+sum_d min(m_d,p). Each unequal unordered position pair contributes to exactly one m_d, so sum_d m_d=M=(n^2-sum_c n_c^2)/2. Also sum_d min(m_d,p)<=sum_d min(n-d,p)=O(n min(n,p)), proving Q=O(n+min{M,n min(n,p)}). The keys are word-sized because p=n^{O(1)}, so constant-pass radix sorting costs O(n+Q). Independently, the compact suffix tree has total edge-length D and one locus per distinct substring content. Walking those edge labels computes all D fingerprints, and sorting (length,fingerprint) detects exactly whether two different contents collide. This route costs O(n log n+n+D). D and M are computable during preprocessing, so choosing the cheaper route yields the stated minimum. Substituting any of p=O(log n), D=O(n log n), or M=O(n log n) gives O(n log n).
claims.witness: An accepting certificate is either p mismatches at one displacement, which forces a repeated field state, or two sorted records with the same (d,state); the latter reconstructs unequal equal-length substrings. In the D route, two distinct contents with the same (length,fingerprint) are the certificate.
claims.search_method: Proved the state-count and unequal-pair identities combinatorially, audited both algorithmic routes and their word-RAM sorting costs, and exhaustively compared their decision characterizations with brute force on 8,898 invertible-base instances using exact arithmetic.

claims.claim: The target has a complete O(n log n) exact solution in the noninvertible case p divides b.
claims.evidence: Since p is prime and p divides b, b is zero modulo p, so every nonempty most-significant-first fingerprint equals its last character modulo p. For endpoints e<f in the same residue class, all aligned substrings ending there are equal exactly when R_e=s[e]...s[0] is a prefix of R_f. If this prefix condition fails first at offset t, the length-(t+1) substrings are unequal but have equal fingerprints. Ordering endpoints increasingly orders the lengths of R_e; therefore, if every consecutive pair in a residue class satisfies the prefix relation, transitivity gives it for every pair, while any consecutive failure supplies a collision. LCP support on the reversed string tests each relation in constant time after O(n log n) preprocessing, and sorting/grouping endpoints by residue stays within O(n log n). Reversing the argument handles the opposite coefficient orientation.
claims.witness: For consecutive same-residue endpoints e<f whose reversed prefixes first differ at offset t, the length-(t+1) substrings ending at e and f are a concrete unequal colliding pair.
claims.search_method: Independent endpoint characterization and transitivity proof, plus exhaustive exact-integer comparison against brute force for 2,966 noninvertible-base instances and both coefficient orientations.

claims.claim: Collisions cannot occur at length L when b^L<=p, but checking only power-of-two lengths, only lexicographically adjacent contents, or relying on monotonicity in the length is insufficient.
claims.evidence: Canonical length-L base-b words are distinct integers in [0,b^L-1]. When b^L<=p, the nonzero difference of two such integers has absolute value below p and cannot be divisible by p. For b=2, p=5, and S=000101, exact fingerprint arrays for lengths 1 through 6 are respectively [0,0,0,1,0,1], [0,0,1,2,1], [0,1,2,0], [1,2,0], [2,0], and [0]. The only unequal-content collision occurs at length 3, between 000 and 101. Thus lengths 1,2,4 are collision-free, collision existence is nonmonotone across lengths, and the colliding contents are nonadjacent in the length-3 lexicographic order 000,001,010,101.
claims.witness: b=2, p=5, S=000101. The length-3 substrings 000 and 101 have integer values 0 and 5 and fingerprint 0 modulo 5, while every other length is collision-free and the two contents are separated lexicographically by 001 and 010.
claims.search_method: Direct injectivity proof and exact-integer enumeration of the stated binary example, supplemented by exhaustive threshold checks throughout all 11,864 tested base/string/prime instances.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for a worst-case linear or O(n log n) detector for an arbitrary supplied string and prime, with a declared small false-rejection probability permitted. The draft completely and exactly handles p dividing b and proves useful structural and adaptive results when p does not divide b. However, its invertible-base running time contains min{D,M,n min(n,p)}, which can be quadratic, and the O(n log n) conclusion is established only under the stated restrictions p=O(log n), D=O(n log n), or M=O(n log n). The final writeup explicitly identifies the remaining general invertible-base case as unresolved and does not claim that probabilistic rejection closes it. These are material but incomplete advances, so VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS is appropriate. The draft's claimed_resolution of PARTIAL is therefore ACCURATE, neither overstated nor understated.
